errors.english: This occurs for the meaning understood as the object
errors.why: དོན་དུ་རྟོགས་པ is implication (arthāpatti): the qualification applies to the meaning understood by implication, not 'understood as the object'.

errors.english: If you say that the very mention of "proving the probandum" is not what makes it a particular, it is not a particular.
errors.why: The objection asks whether the mention of 'proving the probandum' itself is not the qualification (i.e. claims it is), and the reply denies it; the English makes objection and reply say the same thing.

note: The argument is followed in outline, but the objection-and-reply structure and the term for implication are muddled in places.

errors.english: he should bless his mind with the thought
errors.why: Here སེམས་ཀྱིས་བྱིན་གྱིས་བརླབ (adhiṣṭhāna) is the Vinaya act of mentally resolving or determining, not blessing his mind.

fix.find: he should bless his mind with the thought
fix.replace: he should mentally resolve with the thought

errors.english: Sitting naturally
errors.why: The elder should himself get up and be ready (seated in place), a duty of conduct, not 'sitting naturally'.

note: An accurate rendering of the five modes of Prātimokṣa recitation and the reciter's duties, with one Vinaya term mistranslated.

errors.english: This is not the case; if it possessed parts, it would not be a substantial reality.
errors.why: དེ་ལྟ་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ here means 'otherwise': if it had parts it would not be substantially real; the text does not reject the preceding consequence.

note: A sound translation of the argument about the shapes of atoms and the conventional existence of the pot.

errors.english: the crown of Indra's head
errors.why: བརྒྱ་བྱིན་གྱི་སྤྱི་བོ (śakramūrdhan) is the standard Pramāṇa example meaning an anthill, which emits vapour like smoke, not Indra's head literally.

fix.find: When the crown of Indra's head is of a nature that is not fire, at that time, if smoke arises from the crown of Indra's head
fix.replace: When an anthill (lit. 'Indra's head') is of a nature that is not fire, at that time, if smoke arises from the anthill

errors.english: there are only those specific characteristics that have become its own essence
errors.why: The reply says that although fire has particulars, it certainly also has a particular that is its own nature; ཁོ་ན marks emphasis, not 'only those'.

note: The dense argument about fire, smoke and causal specificity is mostly tracked, but the key śakramūrdhan (anthill) example is mistranslated.

errors.english: the object of cognition and the negation of that object are designated as existing because they are present, while their reversal is the non-existence of non-perception. Thus, even the perceived is said to be non-existent.
errors.why: The text says the cognition and its object (the thing to be negated) are what is designated 'existence', their cessation is the absence that is non-perception, and hence absence is also called non-perception; the English turns the negandum into 'the negation' and inverts the conclusion.

errors.english: by using signs that are not incompatible with the body or the mind
errors.why: The Mīmāṃsakas use reasons such as having a body or intellect, which are not incompatible with omniscience; the English makes the signs compatible with the body or mind.

note: The topic of non-perception and the final causal complex comes through, but two key sentences are misconstrued.

errors.english: In this context, being authentic means that non-deceptiveness remains uncontradicted.
errors.why: The Tibetan denies the claim: the absence of anything that defeats non-deceptiveness is not genuine there (in dreams), since in a dream one later experiences that same thing or something else.

errors.english: (Kumarila) [note: refers to the Mimamsa scholar Kumarila Bhatta]
errors.why: The Tibetan does not name Kumārila (his usual Tibetan name is གཞོན་ནུ་མ་ལེན), so the attribution is speculative.

errors.english: is intended to be the producer of its own aspect
errors.why: མངོན་པར་སེམས་པ here is the cognition's (mis)conception (abhimāna) of the object as producing its own image, as the next side's མངོན་པར་རློམ་པ confirms, not 'intended'.

note: The dream-versus-waking and non-perception discussion is partly followed, but there is a likely reversal at the opening and a speculative attribution.

errors.english: such as a lotus from dissimilar kinds like somewhat heavy [mud] and so forth
errors.why: ལྕི་བ is cow dung (the classic example of things arising from a dissimilar kind), not 'heavy [mud]'.

fix.find: such as a lotus from dissimilar kinds like somewhat heavy [mud] and so forth
fix.replace: such as a lotus and so forth from dissimilar kinds like cow dung

errors.english: Otherwise, there would sometimes be no meaning at all.
errors.why: The point is that otherwise its occasional occurrence (sometimes seen, sometimes not) would be impossible, not that 'there would sometimes be no meaning'.

errors.english: If it is of its very nature, there is no error since it is not that very thing.
errors.why: If it has that nature, there is no deviation through something that is not that (cause); the English garbles the logic.

note: The summary verses (with 'anthill' correctly rendered) are fine, but the prose has a mistranslated example and two garbled inferential clauses.

errors.english: These phenomena are neither with affliction nor without affliction.
errors.why: The sūtra says these dharmas are without affliction and are not afflicted; it does not deny that they are without affliction.

fix.find: These phenomena are neither with affliction nor without affliction.
fix.replace: These phenomena are without affliction; they are not afflicted.

note: A good translation of the dharma-smṛtyupasthāna passage and the Akṣayamati quotation, with one reversed clause and heavy inline glossing.

errors.english: there is no downfall in any case for one who possesses a mind lacking the intent to deceive
errors.why: ཡིད་མི་ཆེས་པའི་སེམས means a mind of distrust or disbelief, not 'lacking the intent to deceive'.

errors.english: has no specific purpose [note: to evade], there is no downfall
errors.why: The bracketed notes 'to evade' and 'with intent' impose a reading the Tibetan does not support; the contrast concerns whether a carrier standing on ground inside the boundary is needed.

note: The toll-evasion rulings are rendered serviceably, with an interpretive gloss and one term to correct.

errors.english: the steward (Dumbu dzinpa) Fragment-Holder
errors.why: Nothing in the Tibetan calls Dum bu 'dzin pa a steward; it is just a name.

errors.english: Chandra must be deprived of his charms and completely separated from us.
errors.why: The Tibetan says only that Candra is to be separated from ཡིད་འཕྲོག (charm, or a name); 'from us' is added.

note: The narrative is followed, but the verses and some speeches are loose and there are small additions about the antagonist.
